summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, multiple abdominal surgeries, and short bowel syndrome was admitted with right lower quadrant and flank pain, nausea, vomiting, and fever. Imaging revealed proximal small bowel distension without complete obstruction, consistent with partial small bowel obstruction. A urine culture from an outside hospital grew E. coli, prompting treatment for a urinary tract infection with ampicillin. She was managed conservatively with bowel rest, IV fluids, and pain control. An EGD and colonoscopy showed no active Crohn’s disease or strictures. Her symptoms improved, she tolerated a diet, and was discharged on oral ampicillin, a tapering course of Dilaudid, and short-term oxazepam for anxiety. No complications occurred during the admission.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
